A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReDit study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results on GSM8K, MATH, and Geometry3K, including comparisons across models, RL algorithms, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds coding evaluations, full-parameter fine-tuning experiments, and tests on DeepSeek distilled models in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 4 retain the same procedure: add independent zero-mean Gaussian or uniform noise to rewards before computing normalized advantages and optimizing GRPO. Reward implementations and scheduled perturbations already appear in v1; the added experiments do not introduce a new ReDit component.

E1.justification: v3 retains the three mathematical reasoning datasets and adds code generation in Appendix E.1: APPS training/testing, APPS-trained evaluation on HumanEval, and CodeContests training/testing. This substantially expands domain coverage and introduces cross-dataset coding evaluation.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain GRPO, DAPO, Dr.GRPO, REINFORCE++, Gradient Clipping, and Dynamic Sampling. Removing some numerical tables does not remove their comparisons, which remain plotted. The added Appendix E experiments use the existing GRPO comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds full-parameter fine-tuning using VERL with eight GPUs, GSM8K evaluations of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, and coding evaluation using pass@1. These are additional experimental configurations; the original LoRA/TR L setup, dataset splits, and Appendix D hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices E.2–E.3 add substantial checks of whether ReDit's benefits persist beyond LoRA and on specialized reasoning models. Full fine-tuning is tested across all three original benchmarks. Existing perturbation sensitivity, scheduling, continuous-reward, gradient-manipulation, and training-dynamics analyses remain.

E5.justification: Unlike v1's point estimates, v3 newly reports multiple-run summaries and adds ± terms to ReDit rows in Tables 1–2. Section 5.1 claims five independent runs but lists six settings, including no seed, and labels the reported dispersion 'variance.' The reporting change is clear, although the exact run count and statistical interpretation are ambiguous.

E6.justification: Figures 15–17 add coding, full-fine-tuning, and distilled-model results favoring ReDit under those new conditions. Matched original results remain unchanged: for example, both versions report MATH accuracy of 48.01 for GRPO and 52.55 for Gaussian ReDit. These additions expand the results rather than establish improved performance on reruns of existing settings.

T1.justification: v3 removes Proposition 6.3 and its Appendix B.3 proof, including the noise-dependent convergence-time bounds and reward-ranking accuracy derivation. The unbiased-gradient and gradient-variance propositions and proofs remain. Moving the original accuracy and variance definitions into Appendix B.1 introduces no new theory.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the explicit contribution claim that Proposition 6.3 proves faster convergence, narrowing the stated theoretical contribution to unbiasedness and gradient variance. The principal method claims and abstract's approximately 10% training-step and 4% performance-improvement claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets the results as evidence that benefits extend beyond mathematical reasoning and are not specific to LoRA or ordinary instruction-tuned models. Section 7 strengthens the existing tuning limitation by noting that extensive experimentation remains necessary despite small-dataset search. The original noise-strength and continuous-reward qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Figure 1 newly specifies that gradient norms are measured before clipping, and Appendix E.2 documents VERL and eight-GPU execution. The new checklist states that code and instructions accompany supplementary material, although neither PDF supplies a ReDit access link. Existing reward code and parameter tables are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A replaces explicit differentiation from Spurious Rewards and Random Reward Perturbation with broader reward-shaping context, adding citations such as Ng, Grześ, and Gupta. The RRP citation is removed; Spurious Rewards remains cited in Section 5.1. Several background citations are added, while the central positioning around discrete-reward optimization remains.

P1.justification: Most main-text wording and the seven-section narrative remain. Changes include localized introductory, related-work, and conclusion rewrites; relocating definitions; reorganizing the result appendices; and adding acknowledgements and a conference checklist. Author, affiliation, and venue information also changes.

P2.justification: The two-column ICML layout becomes a single-column NeurIPS layout, extensively reflowing and relocating displays. v3 adds Figures 15–17 and uncertainty terms in the main tables. It removes v1 Tables 11–16 while retaining their corresponding plots, and renumbers several retained figures and tables.

improvement.justification: Appendix E provides useful evidence beyond v1's mathematical reasoning and LoRA evaluations, strengthening support for broader applicability. New uncertainty reporting also helps, but inconsistent run counts, unclear dispersion notation, and sparse details for the added experiments limit its value. Removing detailed numerical tables and the RRP comparison reduces transparency, while the formal contribution becomes narrower. The added validation supports a modest net improvement.
